name: Silt and Filament: Shelf Dispatches 2201-2209
creator: Compiled by Osei Tamboli-Varga; multiple contributors
description: A collected print anthology of zine dispatches written, illustrated, and hand-distributed across Tier 1 neighborhoods over eight years, covering everything from food scarcity riots to the underground chrome-repair economy. Physical copies are assembled from salvaged paper and bound with wire, each one unique; no two are identical. The neural feed version, uploaded illegally in 2211, was stripped of its physical character and is considered by purists to be a pale imitation.
medium: physical (hand-assembled print); pirated neural feed exists but is considered degraded
cultural_impact: Became the definitive primary-source document of Shelf life in the early 2200s, cited by underground historians and occasionally by Tier 3-4 journalists who want credibility without actually visiting the Shelf.
controversy: Two contributors were detained by Meridian Civic Security in 2212 following the neural upload; the compiler Tamboli-Varga has been in legal gray status ever since. Corponation Halvex Media has attempted twice to license the content for a sanitized documentary series.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 journalist buys a physical copy and discovers a dispatch that names a sitting Halvex Media executive in a Shelf arson — information that was scrubbed from the neural version.

One of the detained contributors has been quietly released and is now working inside a corponation; a player character must decide whether they are an informant or a sleeper agent for something larger.
A collector offers an enormous sum for a specific early print run — the one containing a map of unmapped Shelf infrastructure that someone very powerful wants destroyed.
